item: A custody retry-queue line that cannot be read is no longer glued to the next record, dropped unlogged or erased by a rewrite
summary: custody_pending.jsonl is where a custody write that failed at ingest waits, and a full disk or a power cut is what makes a write fail and cuts a queue write short. A line cut short has no newline, so _append put the next record on the same line and both were unreadable (note_failed(4) returned True; read_pending still returned [1, 2]); read_pending skipped any line it could not read without a log record; a line whose bytes were not text raised UnicodeDecodeError out of read_pending; and drain's _rewrite wrote the file back from the records it had read, so the unreadable text was erased for good (and an empty record list unlinked the file). _append now closes a file that ends mid-line first; read_pending reads bytes, treats a line that is not a JSON object with an article_id as unreadable, and logs each such line once per process by line number and byte length (never its text); _rewrite keeps unreadable lines byte for byte in data/custody_pending.unreadable and writes them back into the queue instead if that file cannot be written, so no line is erased unseen. 13 tests drive the real note_failed/read_pending/drain against real files (11 red before, the other 2 are controls); 19 mutants of the new logic, 19 killed. Limits: a queue holding only unreadable lines is not rewritten (drain_owed and drain return early on no records), so the line stays in the queue file and is reported once per process; the unreadable file is plaintext like the queue and is read by no code path; a rewrite that set a line aside and then failed to replace the queue sets it aside again next time (a duplicate in the side file); nothing observed in the field.
